unavailable: traffic views and clones: UNKNOWN (requires repository administration read)
item-level issues and pull requests: UNKNOWN (no engagement file supplied)
caveats: Stars, forks, watchers and downloads are public signals, not active users or adoption.
Maintainer and CI downloads cannot be excluded from public download totals.
An absent value is UNKNOWN; it is never estimated.
Correlation in a short window is not causation; every experiment needs a stated counterfactual.

opportunities.title: Make traffic observable before spending on promotion
opportunities.relevance: Without administration read, views and clones are UNKNOWN, so no channel can be compared and no experiment can be measured. This blocks the whole optimization loop.
opportunities.action: Add a fine-grained METRICS_TOKEN with Administration: read to the existing metrics-daily workflow. Do not broaden the development token.
opportunities.expected_value: Turns every later channel test from unmeasurable into a comparable, 14-day observation.
opportunities.risk: Low: read-only permission; secret handled by the existing workflow secret store.
opportunities.reason: Data-quality note in the snapshot; existing ops/README documents the required permission.

opportunities.title: Produce item-level issue and pull-request evidence
opportunities.relevance: The snapshot counts open issues and PRs but cannot distinguish a meaningful contributor report from noise, so contribution growth stays UNKNOWN.
opportunities.action: Run the documented read-only engagement export and pass it to the weekly analysis. Classify only public item metadata.
opportunities.expected_value: Makes external contribution and showcase participation a measured signal instead of a guess.
opportunities.risk: Low: public metadata only; no private repository content.
opportunities.reason: Engagement input absent from this run; the classification is marked UNKNOWN rather than assumed.

opportunities.title: Reduce review latency for the current pull-request queue
opportunities.audience: external contributors evaluating whether to stay
opportunities.relevance: 8 open pull requests against 1 visible contributor(s) is a first-response risk: a new contributor who waits cannot tell interest from abandonment.
opportunities.action: State a response window in CONTRIBUTING, triage the queue, and close or label stale items with a reason. This is a maintenance action, not a promotion.
opportunities.expected_value: Improves contributor conversion without any new channel spend.
opportunities.risk: Low: maintenance work; do not merge unreviewed changes to hit a number.
opportunities.reason: Open PR and contributor counts from the snapshot.

opportunities.title: Record channel outcomes before scaling any channel
opportunities.relevance: 6 of 6 registered channels have no recorded observation, so the strategy layer has no evidence on which to keep or stop a channel.
opportunities.action: After each authorized action, record date, material and observable result in the channel registry. Leave the result empty when nothing can be observed.
opportunities.expected_value: Prevents effort from accumulating in channels that never worked.

opportunities.title: Check whether release archives are discoverable as a first experience
opportunities.audience: visitors who reach releases but not the README
opportunities.relevance: Cumulative release-asset downloads exceed stars. That is a hypothesis about discoverability, not proof of users; downloads include maintainers and CI.
opportunities.action: Review the release notes first screen and the README entry paths. Do not claim downloads as users and do not buy promotion.
opportunities.expected_value: A clearer first experience for the same traffic already arriving.
opportunities.risk: Low, provided the Fixture/Real AI distinction stays explicit.
opportunities.reason: Snapshot counts only; the causal link to discovery is unproven and labelled as a hypothesis.

experiments.title: README first-screen framing
experiments.hypothesis: If the first screen states the three product differences and the headline 'Create a world. Change it together. Derive something new.', more visitors will recognize the product and follow the repository.
experiments.audience: developers and creators arriving from a search result or a shared link
experiments.change: Update the README first screen and the Showcase entry once, then keep them stable for the whole window.

experiments.title: Derive Relay participation
experiments.hypothesis: If a reproducible base world and five derivation prompts are published together, at least one creator will submit a public derived world through the existing showcase form.
experiments.audience: creators who already build worlds and stories
experiments.change: Publish the Derive Relay material and link it from the Showcase. Do not pre-write or seed submissions.

experiments.title: Developer technical introduction
experiments.hypothesis: If a technically framed introduction is published on an authorized developer channel, at least one external engineer will open a substantive issue or pull request.
experiments.audience: engineers evaluating the runtime, permissions and lineage model
experiments.change: Publish one technical introduction that cites repository paths and reproducible commands. No cross-posting of identical text.
